summary: Tatsugen Sato (1924–2017) was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Komazawa University (~1952–1978). He spent much of his career at Komazawa University, serving as an assistant professor (~1965–1995) and professor (~1976–1995), alongside appointments at Tokai and Ryukoku universities.

Tatsuo Hayashi (1896–1984) studied at Kyoto University (~1917–1921) and worked in philosophy and other fields. He held academic posts at Toyo University (~1925–1932) and Tsuda University (~1948–1965), as well as Meiji, Rikkyo, and Hosei universities.

Tatsuo Nishida (1928–2012), a scholar of linguistics, Sinology, and Tibetology, studied at Kyoto University. His main appointments included serving as a professor and dean at Kyoto University, as president of the Linguistic Society of Japan, and at the National Center for Science Information Systems.

Tatsushi Tamai is a scholar in Iranian and Central Asian studies, Indology, and linguistics. He served as a visiting researcher at the International Research Institute for Advanced Buddhology at Soka University (attested 2010–2016).

Tavivat Puntarigvivat (b. 1950) works in Buddhist studies, religious studies, and philosophy. He studied at the University of Hawaiʻi and under Luangpor Teean Jittasubho, later holding posts at Kyoto University, Mahidol University (attested 2005), and the World Buddhist University (attested 2013).

Taw Sein Ko (1864–1930) was a scholar in history, archaeology, and Indology. He completed his studies at the University of Rangoon (~1881–1882), the Inner Temple (~1892–1893), and Inns of Court (~1892–1893).

Teizo Iyanaga (1915–1983) was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Japanology who studied at the University of Tokyo (~1937–1940). He held posts at Nagoya University (~1949–1950), the University of Tokyo (~1950–1976), and Sophia University (~1976–1983).
Tej Ram Sharma (b. 1941) is an Indologist and historian who earned his doctorate from Banaras Hindu University in 1968. He held a post at Himachal Pradesh University (attested 1978).
Tendzin Chökyi Gyatso studied under the 14th Dalai Lama and Lobsang Gyatso, and also taught Lobsang Gyatso.
Tenga Rinpoche (1932–2012) was a Buddhist studies and Tibetology figure who studied at Benchen Monastery, which he later founded in 1976. He served as Dorje Lopön at Rumtek Monastery (~1967–1984).

Tensei Kitabatake (1928–2024) was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Ryukoku University (~1951–1955). He spent decades at Ryukoku University, becoming a professor (1970) and president (1995–1999), and later served as president of Gifu Shotoku Gakuen University (1999–2005).
Tenshin Tanouye (1938–2003) was active in religious and Buddhist studies. He studied under Sogen Omori, whom he succeeded, and founded Daihonzan Chozen-ji.
Tenzin is a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies who earned a Master of Philosophy at the University of Oslo under the supervision of Hanna Havnevik (attested 2008).

Tenzin Dhargye (b. 1968) studied at Sera Monastery and Gyume Tantric College, and under Ling Rinpoche. In Tibetology and Buddhist studies, he taught at Sera, Gyume, and the University of Virginia, and became director of Tibetzentrum Österreich in 2008.

Tenzin Dorjee is a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar who studied under Geshe Sonam Rinchen, Geshe Lobsang Tsephel, and Geshe Dawa. He worked as a translator at the Library of Tibetan Works and Archives and served at Pullahari Monastery.
Tenzin L. Mullin works in religious studies and Japanology and earned a Master of Arts degree at the University of Otago under the supervision of Elizabeth Guthrie.

Tenzin Wangyal Rinpoche (b. 1961), working in Tibetology and Buddhist studies, studied at Menri Monastery and under Lopon Sangye Tenzin and Yongdzin Tenzin Namdak. He directed the Dialectic School of Menri (~1986–1990) and founded Ligmincha International.

Ter Ellingson (b. 1944) is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies who studied at Concordia College, the University of Chicago, and the University of Wisconsin-Madison (1979). He served as a professor of music at the University of Washington from 1981 to 2016.

Terese Tse Bartholomew, a specialist in history, archaeology, Tibetology, and Sinology, earned an M.A. at the University of California, Los Angeles. She served as Curator of Himalayan Art and Chinese Decorative Art at the Asian Art Museum (attested 2001–2003).

Terrell Carver (b. 1946) is a philosopher who studied at Columbia University (~1964–1968) and the University of Oxford (~1968–1975). He held appointments at the University of Liverpool (~1974–1979) and the University of Bristol (from ~1979).
